operatorApproval.notes:
main moved five commits while X11 was landing: four platform fixes to tests this branch had been reporting as failing (#630 case-only corpus refusal, #631 the 300 ms plannotator race, #633 the herdr outbox perf ratio) and #632, the operator's own landing of the X08 common-directory guard, landed independently of this branch. `git merge-tree --write-tree` produced one tree and zero CONFLICT lines, `git merge` said "Automatic merge went well" -- and `npm run typecheck:core` then failed with TS2323/TS2393: two exported implementations of resolveCommonDir in src/git/GitRepo.ts, 256 and 308, with GitRepo's own class doc comment dropped between them. A conflict-free textual merge cannot see that: main added the guard (#632) and this branch added the guard plus X09's error-context fix, at the same place in a file the merge base had neither in. The resolution keeps one -- the branch's, the superset, because X09 wraps discoverRepo so an EACCES/ESTALE/EIO out of discovery is reported with git's answer and the cause instead of being misreported as "resolves to nothing usable" -- and keeps main's provenance line ("Landed from PR #616 as unit X08") in the surviving doc comment. test/unit/git-common-dir-repair.test.ts was already identical on both sides (`git diff origin/main HEAD -- <that file>` empty before the merge), so nothing in the tests needed reconciling. X12's own content change: 8 insertions / 52 deletions, one file.

Then the numbers were taken again with the command the repository actually gates on, because they had not been before. `npm test` is `node --test --test-concurrency=4 --test-force-exit --import ./test/support/isolatedState.ts "test/unit/**/*.test.ts" "test/integration/**/*.test.ts"`; the X-series tallies (X08, X09, X10) were taken with `npx tsx --test` and no preload. Whole suite at 4be00c17, with --test-timeout=180000 as a bound: 7964 tests, 7956 pass, 3 fail, 0 cancelled, 15m26s (02-whole-suite-canonical-at-4be00c17.txt). The three failing leaves are mission-reliability-foundation (#630's territory), herdr outbox perf ratio and worktree-janitor; each fails identically at origin/main's tip e7888752 run in a separate checkout (02-three-leaves-at-origin-main-e7888752.txt), so they are pre-existing on main and not branch damage. With --test-force-exit the suite terminates: X10's "the suite does not terminate" is not a property of this branch either.

The correction X10's record needs, and why it is recorded rather than quietly re-measured. X10/logs/05 reported worker-budget-build-hint.test.ts failing 2 of 3 copies at --test-concurrency=4 on the branch, passing alone and at origin/main, and carried it as merge-blocking. It was my method. Same four files, same concurrency, branch tip: with the preload and --test-force-exit, 55 pass / 0 fail in 47.7 s, exit 0; with `npx tsx --test --test-timeout=180000` and neither, one leaf lands on the 180 s ceiling (180017.59 ms) and the process has to be killed at 2400 s (03-four-files-gate-invocation.txt, 03-four-files-no-preload-stall.txt). The file passes alone and as three copies under both commands (03-budget-hint-*.txt). The leaf asserts elapsed milliseconds against a 10 s budget, so it is genuinely sensitive to what shares the process' state directory with it, and test/support/isolatedState.ts is what stops that sharing. X10/CORRECTION.md carries the pointer; X10/out and X10/out-chain stay byte-unchanged and hash-bound, because rewriting a hash-bound record would break the X10 -> X11 lineage links X11 exists to police.

Lint parity, restated with the repository's own command rather than the scoped check X10 used. `npm run lint` at the branch tip: exit 1, 516 errors over 488 files (04-lint-npm-branch.txt). `npm run lint` at origin/main tip e7888752 in a separate checkout: exit 0 (04-lint-npm-main.txt). By extension: json 365, ts 118, mjs 5. By area: 365 in docs/specs/harness-reliability-bootstrap-20261103 (the evidence tree), then test/unit 66, src/incidents 15, src/bootstrap 8, src/inference 6, src/aps 4. Rules: 15 analyzer errors (useSingleVarDeclarator 8, useTemplate 3, useImportType 2, useOptionalChain 1, noAssignInExpressions 1) and roughly 500 formatter findings, mechanically fixable. The 365 JSON findings are the decision, and they are not fixable by formatting: they are captured command output and handoff records whose bytes are hashed -- evidence[].sha256 in 99 records, stdoutSha256 in the commands, handoffHash over each record's canonical serialisation -- and AUDIT/integrity-scan.mjs checks only that referenced evidence exists and is tracked (grep 'sha256' finds no re-hashing at lines 52-56/91), so formatting them would make the trail unverifiable and nothing in the current tooling would notice. biome.json already excludes two files for exactly that reason (test/fixtures/backpressure-conformance-v1.json, test/fixtures/mission-snapshot-v3.golden.json -- golden artifacts, because formatting a golden file destroys what it is golden for). Options for the operator are in 04/06 of these logs, in the order I would take them: format the 123 code files and add the evidence tree to files.ignore with that reason; or format code only and file the config question; or merge as-is and take main from exit 0 to exit 1 with 516 findings. The first changes the lint contract for a whole subtree, so it is the operator's call, not a unit's.

A mistake made and caught during authoring, recorded because it is the same class X11 declared. The first X12/fixtures/manifest.json carried a hand-typed baseSha (308935c0e0c5f0f0e1a1d1a4d0e0d0a9d1d1c0a0 -- the right 8 characters and 32 invented ones) and a truncated parentHandoffHash. Both were replaced by values read from git and from X11/out (now X11/out-chain) before the record was emitted, and the generator asserts manifest.baseSha == measured base, the merge's first parent == baseSha, and the resolution's parent == the merge, so an invented pointer cannot become a record. templates/handoff.schema.json still types baseSha/resultSha as plain strings and does not require parentHandoffHash at all (required: specVersion, taskId, status, repo, baseSha, resultSha, taskAuthorityHash, changedFiles, commands, evidence, nextTaskId, nextBaseSha, blockedReasons, operatorApproval, handoffHash), which is why the emit-time asserts are the only thing between a typed typo and a hash-bound record. That schema pattern stays the operator's residual, carried unchanged from X11.
